Seconding the TF2 recommendation. There's also Counter-Strike (Source or Global Offensive), which has a varied playerbase with a lot of hardcore and casual players.

As far as games similar to the game you describe, you could look into Blacklight Retribution, but thats gotten a little pay to win sadly.

I also recommend Star Wars Battlefront 2. It should have no problem with integrated graphics, and has a very active multiplayer community. That said you need a third party program called Gameranger for the multiplayer as the Gamespy shutdown left a lot of games without multiplayer.

I considered suggesting Global Offensive, but it should be noted you can't turn off the post processing effects (due to potential competitive advantages). This could be an issue combined with the integrated graphics.

ioquake3, this is the continuously developed fork of the open sourced quake 3 engine, it works on all modern operating systems and runs on my HD4000 with 400-700 FPS. What's missing is one file called pak0.pk3 that is to be copied into the game folder - you can find that file on one of those quake3 CDs that everyone's got laying around (or you search it on the internet, it's not that hard to find).

Here is why I recommend Quake 3 even though you asked for something "casual": You can hop in, play one match for 3 minutes and hop out again. I have been playing it like this against bots for years in order to gain focus and to concentrate. Before learning for uni I play two to three rounds of Quake3 to get in a concentrated mood and then start working very effectively. It's also one of those games that you can play for weeks and suddenly you jump to a new skill level during one match and have a great sense of achievement because from there on you'll play much better than before. I have been playing it for over a year like this at least several times a week and I still discover new techniques every now and then without actively investing time. You just get better through playing it and it feels rather rewarding.

And then you see a video on youtube of someone playing actually good and you lose your shit. It's a worthwhile experience, try it out.

Team Fortress 2 - it runs on anything and is extremely casual. I typically play as an Engineer because my latency isn't so good - so I can let me sentry do the dirty work for me, because I don't need a uber low ping to be able to repair it.
